I (and I'm positive it's the same for a lot of you as well) seem to run into this comment chain all the time: one person says something reaction worthy, gets the appropriate reaction, then op claims responder is stupid because he a clearly using sarcasm. I know you've seen this, and hope you aren't the op in this particular situation.

Sarcasm is a vocal nuance. The qualities of sarcasm can and are best presented in the spoken word and are "manifested chiefly by vocal inflections" (Wikipedia, but that is a great way to put it) The words aren't sarcastic, the tone is. You don't get to be arrogant and defensive when someone doesn't catch on to your attempt at sarcasm when you use text as a medium for displaying it.

If, for example, (one of countless possibilities, so perhaps not the best one, but still the one I'm going with) there is a video posted where someone is injured in a car accident, and your reply is along the lines of, "well he got what he deserved." That isn't internet worthy sarcasm. When spoken, you could use the proper inflection necessary for those listening to know that you were not being serious. Online that's dry; void of any indication that you are kidding in any way. I'm kind of bummed when I see the "/s" at the end of a comment because that just feels snarky and doesn't properly convey the humor intended by the person posting it, but I appreciate it nonetheless because it helps me to understand exactly where they are coming from and what they are trying to achieve.

Why do I bring this up? Because it seems that every couple of days I see a post lambasting the people from the hate subs on this site which claim they are responsible for curtailing the potential for reasonable discussion in the various sub verses, with the greatest focus being on major ones like v/news. I'm not blind to it, but you can downvoat if you feel the need and those go away; at least they are being upfront with their opinion, so if you disagree you know that right from page one. What kills the conversation for me? When I take the time to respond to someone's opinion that catches my eye, whether I agree or don't, only to have them retort with "I was being sarcastic, idiot." No amount of comments filled with hate, nonsense, or downright misinformation turn me away from a conversation faster than someone flippantly commenting without taking the time to craft a proper response. Derailing the conversation with seemingly real responses is not only more common but more destructive than the clearly real responses filled with toxic words.

Endlessly, it seems that I see posts bemoaning the lack of 'real discussions' on Voat. And yet so much more often then an opportunity to discuss anything do I see one-liners or posts meant to be sarcastic that simply fail to do so. If you aren't one of the ones looking to have debates or real discussions, I suppose this doesn't effect you. But if you are, you need to be willing to put in the effort of clearly stating your opinion in the hopes that others will engage you in thoughtful conversation that may be about topics you don't feel comfortable discussing with friends or family; all of our opinions are valid as they are expressions of our beliefs and it's nice to have a safe space to share those as judgement free as possible. Bottling that shit up leads to some pretty negative outcomes.

My main point here, I suppose, is not to avoid sarcasm; it's a useful a valid form of expression that has a purpose unique to it. Just remember that it is primarily vocal. If you choose to leave a sarcastic comment, great, but remember if it looks real, there is no legitimate way for anyone reading it to tell the difference. U.S. The "/s" thing or lay it on really thick. One line isn't good enough; make multiple attempts using language clearly reserved for people who would share your actually views in the same comment. Aim for more sardonic than sarcastic. This won't clear up all misconceptions; that likely isn't an attainable goal. But if you're one of the ones who would like this to be a space of open, honest discussions, you need to go deeper in your comments and responses than we currently do.
Be more careful when using sarcasm online.
